# Implementation Plan: Codex Fork One-Liner Installer (D-002, Cloudflare R2)

<!-- ralph-meta {"overviewTaskId":"codex-fork-install-script"} -->

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-06-05 from brainstorm `codex-fork-install-script` (operator-selected direction **D-002**). Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan D:/harness-efforts/codexu/.ralph/jobs/codex-fork-install-script/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Deliver a Claude-Code-style one-liner installer for the **Windows-x64 codex fork**:
`irm https://codex.evyatar.dev/install.ps1 | iex`. The installer downloads the existing
`codex-<ver>-win32-x64.tgz` release tarball from **Cloudflare R2 bound to codex.evyatar.dev**,
verifies its SHA-256 against a manifest served from the same origin, extracts the multi-binary
vendor tree to a user install dir, wires the launcher onto PATH itself (codex has **no `install`
subcommand**), kills any running `codex`/`codex-core` first (Windows file-locking), and triggers
the launcher's normal first-run. Re-running the one-liner performs an idempotent in-place upgrade.

A per-release publish step computes the tarball SHA-256, writes `manifest.json` + a `/latest`
version pointer, and uploads the tarball + sha256 + manifest + latest to R2. That single `/latest`
endpoint is also the public version source the redirect plan
(`codex-redirect-upstream-install-update-paths-to-fork`) can curl for its `codex doctor` probe.

This is the operator's **D-002** decision (R2 on their own domain; the brainstorm recommended
D-001, a public GitHub mirror, which the operator declined). The Unix `curl ... | sh` half is a
**Windows-only stub** because the fork builds Windows-x64 only.

**The plan deliberately separates operator/ops-driven infra steps (R2 bucket, DNS, CI/dev
credential) from code-driven steps (scripts, manifest/latest generation, publish-flow edit,
optional Worker).** See `## Infra Prerequisites` and the per-AC `[infra]` / `[code]` tags.

## Research Findings

### Codebase Context

- **Release artifact + publish flow** — `codex/.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml` (tag-triggered `v*`,
  `runs-on: windows-latest`, `RELEASE_TARGET=x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`): builds `codex`, `codex-core`,
  `codex-windows-sandbox-setup`, `codex-command-runner` (L109-130), assembles the vendor layout +
  verified `rg.exe` (L132-154), and builds the merged bundle `codex-${RELEASE_VERSION}-win32-x64.tgz`
  via `npm pack` (L228-252, `$BUNDLE_ASSET`), then `gh release upload ... --clobber` (L254-267,
  `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`). The tarball internal layout is
  `package/vendor/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/codex/{codex.exe,codex-core.exe,codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe,codex-command-runner.exe}`,
  `package/vendor/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/path/rg.exe`, and `package/bin/codex.js`.
- **Manual release path** — `codex/.claude/commands/publish-sandbox-patch.md` **Step 5** (L292-379;
  tarball pack L336-352; `gh release create ... codex-${NEW_VERSION}-win32-x64.tgz` L370-373). This is
  the **authoritative real release path today because gim-home Actions are org-policy-blocked**
  (`escalate-gim-home-actions-policy`). `gh auth switch` is already used here (L239, L273).
- **Current install docs** — `codex/docs/workflows/install.md`: authenticated only
  (`gh auth login` -> `gh release download v<VERSION> --repo gim-home/codex` -> `npm install -g`).
  First-run: shell prompt -> `~/.codex-copilot/config.toml` -> `codex login --provider copilot` ->
  `codex-core.exe`. `codex/docs/README.md` also carries an install pointer.
- **Launcher behavior** — `codex.exe` is the launcher (`codex-rs-overlay/codex-copilot-launcher/`);
  `discovery.rs:3` requires `codex-core.exe` next to `codex.exe`; `setup.rs:16` first-run writes
  `~/.codex-copilot/config.toml`. The **config dir `~/.codex-copilot/` is separate from the binary
  install dir** -> no conflict with installing binaries under `~/.codex-fork/`.
- **The `rg.exe` PATH dependency (load-bearing)** — `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-cli/bin/codex.js:78`
  (the npm shim) prepends the vendor `path/` dir (containing `rg.exe`) to the **child** PATH before
  launching codex. Our installer puts `codex.exe` directly on PATH, **bypassing the JS shim**, so
  `rg.exe` will NOT be discoverable unless we co-locate it on the same PATH-visible dir.
- **Standalone-layout alternative** — `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/install-context/src/lib.rs:184`
  detects a standalone package under `~/.codex/packages/standalone/releases/...` with
  `codex-package.json`, `bin/`, `codex-resources/`, `codex-path/`. Adopting that layout would let
  `codex doctor`/update actions classify the install natively (see Open Questions).
- **Script home** — there is no `codex/scripts/` dir today. Upstream's OWN install scripts at
  `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/scripts/install/install.{ps1,sh}` are **reference-only**
  (upstream-canonical, single-binary openai/codex model) — our installer is **net-new wrapper-owned**,
  reusing patterns (`Invoke-WithInstallLock`, `Path-Contains`/`Prepend-PathEntry`, staging-before-move,
  checksum verification) but not editing the upstream files.
- **Redirect-plan coupling (out of scope here)** — `codex-rs/cli/src/doctor/updates.rs:24-26`
  (`GITHUB_LATEST_RELEASE_URL`) and `tui/src/update_action.rs:17` (install-hint string) are repointed
  by `codex-redirect-upstream-install-update-paths-to-fork`; this plan only documents the `/latest`
  contract those edits consume.

### Technical Constraints

- **Windows-x64 only.** No Unix `RELEASE_TARGET` exists; `install.sh` must be a non-zero stub.
- **Multi-binary npm tarball**, not a bare `.exe`: the installer must extract
  `package/vendor/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/**` (use built-in `tar.exe`).
- **No `install` subcommand** -> the script owns PATH wiring.
- **Windows file-locking**: a running `codex`/`codex-core` holds the `.exe` open; must terminate first.
- **Version shape** `0.135.0-copilot-api.1`: the version-guard regex must accept the `-copilot-api.N`
  suffix (the upstream installer's regex does not).
- **`rg.exe` co-location** is required (see above) since the JS shim is bypassed.
- **CI vs manual drift**: the manual Step 5 and CI workflow are not identical; the R2-upload logic
  must be a single shared implementation invoked by both to avoid manifest drift. Codex research
  flagged a possible Step 5 binary-set drift to verify before wiring (see Risk Areas / Open Questions).
- **Trust model**: serving manifest + bytes from the same R2 origin is acceptable under single-origin
  TLS that the operator controls (this is the operator's stated D-002 trust posture).
- **R2 is new infra**: no repo dependency on `wrangler` exists today; bucket/DNS/credential are
  operator-owned.

## Approach

### Architecture

A **single shared release-publisher helper** (wrapper-owned, under `codex/scripts/release/`) is the
contract owner: given `(version, bundle-tarball-path, base-url, bucket-config)` it computes SHA-256 +
size, writes `manifest.json` and `latest`, and uploads `{tarball, tarball.sha256, manifest.json,
latest}` to R2. **It additionally publishes/syncs the installer scripts themselves** —
`install.ps1` and `install.sh` to the R2 root keys `/install.ps1` and `/install.sh` — because the
one-liner `irm https://codex.evyatar.dev/install.ps1 | iex` depends on those static objects existing
and matching the repo source. Both the manual `publish-sandbox-patch.md` Step 5 (primary today) and
the CI `publish-npm.yml` (pending Actions unblock) call this one helper, so the manifest and the
served scripts can never diverge between paths.

**R2 upload interface (decided default):** the helper uses **`wrangler r2 object put`** (env
`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` + `R2_ACCOUNT_ID` + `R2_BUCKET`) — Cloudflare-native, handles R2 auth itself,
**no hand-rolled signing**. The S3-compatible alternative (env `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/
`R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`/`R2_ACCOUNT_ID`|`R2_S3_ENDPOINT`/`R2_BUCKET`) requires **AWS SigV4 signing** —
a plain HTTP PUT to R2 fails — so it must pull a signer dependency (`aws4fetch` (tiny) or
`@aws-sdk/client-s3`); the repo has no existing R2 helper to reuse, so the dependency choice is part of
US-001. **Credential-absence behavior is path-dependent (see F-012 fix):** in the CI `publish-npm.yml`
step the helper **no-ops non-fatally** when creds are absent (safe pre-credential); on the manual
`publish-sandbox-patch.md` Step 5 — the authoritative release path — a missing credential is a **hard
failure by default** (so a release can never publish the GitHub asset while leaving the R2 one-liner
broken) unless `--skip-r2` or `--dry-run` is explicitly passed. A `--dry-run`/`--local-out` mode writes
the manifest + sha256 locally for tests without network.

**`wrangler` availability + publish ordering (helper contract):** neither `publish-npm.yml` nor the
manual `publish-sandbox-patch.md` currently sets up `wrangler`, so the helper must not assume a global
install — it invokes a **pinned `npx -y wrangler@<pinned>`** (Node is present on both `windows-latest`
CI and the dev box), and **prerequisite-checks** wrangler+network reachability up front, hard-failing
the manual path with a clear message when unavailable (the CI path stays the documented no-op).
**Partial-publish ordering is mandatory:** the helper uploads `{tarball, tarball.sha256, manifest.json,
install.ps1, install.sh}` FIRST, verifies each upload succeeded, and writes **`/latest` LAST** — so a
failed or partial publish can never leave `/latest` pointing at a version whose manifest or tarball is
missing (which would break `install.ps1`). On any pre-`/latest` failure the helper aborts without
touching `/latest`.

**Install layout (decided default, operator-overridable) — note the self-update consequence:**
install under `~/.codex-fork/` structured to satisfy `codex`'s own install-context detection where
possible: binaries in `~/.codex-fork/bin/{codex.exe, codex-core.exe, codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe,
codex-command-runner.exe, rg.exe}` plus a `codex-package.json` marker at `~/.codex-fork/`, and add
`~/.codex-fork/bin` (not the root) to user PATH. **`rg.exe` MUST be co-located in that on-PATH `bin/`
dir** because running `codex.exe` directly bypasses the `bin/codex.js` shim that normally prepends the
vendor `path/` dir. **Consequence to verify (US-003):** `install-context/src/lib.rs` classifies an
install as `package_layout` / standalone or `Other`; for `Other`, `tui/src/update_action.rs:25`
returns `UpdateAction::None`, i.e. **native `codex` self-update is disabled**. US-003 must verify
whether the `~/.codex-fork/bin` + `codex-package.json` shape is classified as a recognized layout. If
install-context's detection is anchored to a fixed root (e.g. `~/.codex/packages/standalone/releases/`)
that `~/.codex-fork/` cannot satisfy, then **native self-update is an accepted v1 limitation** — the
upgrade path is re-running the one-liner — tracked as a follow-up (add install-context support for
`.codex-fork`, or adopt the standalone layout). The operator may instead choose Option 2 up front
(install under `~/.codex/packages/standalone/releases/<ver>/` so doctor/update work natively).


The **static R2 object model** is used (recommended over a Cloudflare Worker for v1): `/latest`,
`/<ver>/manifest.json`, `/releases/<ver>/codex-<ver>-win32-x64.tgz` (+`.sha256`), `/install.ps1`,
`/install.sh` are all plain objects under `codex.evyatar.dev`. A Worker is an optional follow-up if
single-origin routing/redirects (or serving the doctor probe with logic) are later desired.

`install.ps1` follows the `claude.ai/install.ps1` flow adapted for a multi-binary tarball with no
`install` subcommand, and **owns PATH wiring + `rg.exe` co-location** itself.

### Implementation Strategy

**Prerequisite decisions (resolve BEFORE US-003 begins):** the **install layout** (flat
`~/.codex-fork/bin` vs upstream standalone) and the **manifest URL shape** (direct custom-domain vs
Worker-proxied) must be fixed first — they are inputs the installer and docs bake in, and changing
them after US-003 forces rework. The defaults above are the starting point; flag in US-001/US-003 if
the install-context verification forces a layout change.

Ordered so the contract (manifest/latest shape) is fixed first, then consumers:

1. **Release-publisher helper** (defines manifest.json + /latest shape; uploads release objects AND
   the install scripts; testable in dry-run/local mode).
2. **Publish-flow wiring** — manual Step 5 first (real path; ALSO fix its binary set), CI workflow
   second (guarded, pending secret/Actions unblock).
3. **`install.ps1`** (consumes the manifest/latest contract; verifies install-context classification).
4. **`install.sh` stub** (independent).
5. **`/latest` endpoint + doctor-probe contract doc** (+ optional Worker source).
6. **Docs** — `install.md` one-liner primary, `docs/README.md` pointer, infra runbook, redirect coupling.

### Files to Create/Modify

**Create (wrapper-owned, zero upstream-conflict surface):**
- `codex/scripts/release/publish-r2.mjs` (or `.sh`) — shared sha256+size compute, manifest.json +
  latest write, R2 upload of the release objects, **and upload/sync of `install.ps1` + `install.sh`
  to the R2 root keys `/install.ps1` `/install.sh`**. Single source of manifest + served-script truth.
  No-ops with a clear message + `--dry-run`/`--local-out` mode when R2 creds are absent.
- `codex/scripts/install.ps1` — real Windows installer (algorithm below). (Served at
  `codex.evyatar.dev/install.ps1`; repo path is decoupled from served key — the helper uploads it.)
- `codex/scripts/install.sh` — Windows-only non-zero stub.
- `codex/scripts/worker/` *(optional, deferred)* — Cloudflare Worker source if the Worker `/latest`
  option is chosen.

**Modify:**
- `codex/.claude/commands/publish-sandbox-patch.md` — **(a) reconcile the binary set** (Step 5 L304
  currently copies only `codex.exe`+`codex-core.exe`; add `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` and
  `codex-command-runner.exe` so it matches CI's `publish-npm.yml` L139-142 — otherwise the R2 bundle
  is incomplete); **(b)** call `publish-r2.mjs` after the tarball is packed (after ~L352, before the
  `gh release create` at ~L370); **PRIMARY upload path**.
- `codex/.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml` — add an R2-upload step after `$BUNDLE_ASSET` is set
  (after ~L252), guarded so it no-ops when the R2 secret is absent; **pending until Actions unblocked**.
- `codex/docs/workflows/install.md` — make the one-liner the primary unauthenticated install; retain
  the authenticated `gh release download` path as the documented fallback/internal path.
- `codex/docs/README.md` — point the quick-install at the one-liner.

**install.ps1 algorithm (precise):**
1. `GET https://$BaseUrl/latest`; reject unless body matches the version guard
   `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-copilot-api\.\d+)?$` (HTML/error-page guard).
2. `GET https://$BaseUrl/<version>/manifest.json` -> `{ version, "win32-x64": { url, sha256, size } }`.
3. Download the tarball to a temp path.
4. `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256` -> compare to manifest `sha256`; on mismatch **delete temp, abort,
   make NO PATH/install-dir changes**.
5. **Scoped process-kill:** stop ONLY running `codex`/`codex-core` processes whose executable path is
   under the target install root (`$CODEX_INSTALL_ROOT`/`~/.codex-fork/`) — do NOT blanket-kill every
   `codex` process (an unrelated npm-global install or active session elsewhere must be left alone).
   When interactive (no `CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE`), prompt before terminating; otherwise terminate
   target-scoped processes automatically.
6. **Safe swap:** extract with `tar.exe -xzf` into a staging dir; lay out
   `bin/{codex.exe, codex-core.exe, codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe, codex-command-runner.exe, rg.exe}`
   + a `codex-package.json` marker. Then **backup** the current install dir, **rename** staging into
   place, and on any failure **roll back** from the backup (replacing a non-empty Windows directory is
   not atomic — this stage->backup->rename->rollback sequence prevents leaving the user with no working
   install). `rg.exe` MUST land in the on-PATH `bin/` dir.
7. Wire PATH **for both new and the current session**: (a) persist user-scope
   `[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path', <updated>, 'User')`, adding `~/.codex-fork/bin`
   exactly once (no duplicates; remove any stale prior entry first) — this is what NEW shells inherit;
   AND (b) prepend `~/.codex-fork/bin` to `$env:Path` in the **current** PowerShell session, because a
   `irm ... | iex` one-liner runs in the user's live session and a child process inherits the parent's
   process env (NOT the just-written registry value) — without (b), `codex` would not be runnable until
   a new shell is opened.
8. Trigger the launcher's first-run (skip when `CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE`; then instruct the user to
   run `codex`).
9. Idempotent upgrade = re-run = re-stage + backup + rename; clean up the temp tarball + backup on
   success.
- Testability knobs: `CODEX_INSTALL_ROOT` (override `~/.codex-fork/`), `CODEX_BASE_URL` (point at a
  local/stub origin), `CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE` (scope-kill without prompt + skip the first-run launch).

## Scope

### In Scope (code-driven, Ralph-implementable)
- The shared release-publisher helper (manifest.json + latest + sha256 + R2 upload of release objects
  **and** of `install.ps1`/`install.sh` to the R2 root).
- Reconciling the manual Step 5 binary set (add the 2 missing exes) and wiring the helper into manual
  Step 5 (primary) and CI publish-npm.yml (guarded/pending).
- `install.ps1` (real, with scoped process-kill + stage/backup/rename/rollback + layout verification),
  `install.sh` (Windows-only stub).
- The static-R2 `/latest` + manifest contract and a doctor-probe contract note for the redirect plan.
- Docs updates (`install.md`, `docs/README.md`) + the infra-vs-code runbook section.

### Out of Scope
- Creating the R2 bucket / DNS binding / CI credential (operator/ops — see Infra Prerequisites).
- Any Unix build target (`install.sh` stays a stub until a Unix `RELEASE_TARGET` is added).
- D-001 (public GitHub mirror — operator declined), D-003 (dev-box tunnel — rejected), D-004
  (authenticated-only — superseded by the D-002 decision).
- Implementing the redirect plan's edits to `doctor/updates.rs` / `tui/update_action.rs` /
  US-003 hint strings — this plan only documents the `/latest` contract they consume.
- A Cloudflare Worker (optional follow-up; static objects ship first).

## Infra Prerequisites (operator/ops-driven — NOT Ralph-implementable)

These gate end-to-end validation but NOT code authoring. They are an operator runbook, surfaced so
the impl member does not attempt them:
1. **Create the R2 bucket** + a retention/lifecycle policy (~100 MB/release accumulates on the 10 GB
   free tier; decide how many releases to keep and whether pruning is manual or part of the publish
   step).
2. **Bind `codex.evyatar.dev`** to the bucket (Cloudflare custom domain or Worker route) and serve
   `install.{ps1,sh}` from that origin.
3. **Provision the R2 credential** — an S3-compatible access-key-id + secret (or scoped API token,
   least-privilege = write to the one bucket): a GitHub Actions secret for CI **and/or** a dev-box
   env var for the manual `/publish-sandbox-patch` path. Document where it lives and its rotation.

## Risk Areas
- **Windows file-locking on upgrade** — a running `codex`/`codex-core` blocks overwrite; mitigated by
  the **scoped** process-kill (only exes under the install root) + staged swap.
- **Non-atomic Windows directory replacement** — renaming/replacing a non-empty install dir can fail
  partway and leave no working install; mitigated by the stage->backup->rename->rollback sequence.
- **Over-broad process-kill** — blanket-killing every `codex` process could terminate an unrelated
  npm-global install or another active session; mitigated by scoping to exes under the install root
  and prompting unless `CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE`.
- **Native self-update disabled by layout** — if the `~/.codex-fork/` shape is classified `Other` by
  `install-context/src/lib.rs`, `tui/src/update_action.rs:25` returns `UpdateAction::None`, so
  `codex` cannot self-update; mitigated by structuring the install as a recognized layout (verify in
  US-003) or accepting the re-run-the-one-liner upgrade path as a documented v1 limitation + follow-up.
- **`rg.exe` not on PATH** — bypassing `bin/codex.js` drops the shim's PATH-prepend; mitigated by
  co-locating `rg.exe` in the on-PATH `bin/` dir (hard AC).
- **`tar.exe` / `.tgz` extraction quirks** on Windows (nested `package/` prefix; symlink/permission
  edge cases) — verify extraction yields `package/vendor/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/**`.
- **Incomplete published bundle** — the manual Step 5 currently packs only 2 of 4 binaries; the R2
  bundle our installer extracts would be missing `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` +
  `codex-command-runner.exe` unless Step 5 is reconciled (US-002, hard requirement) and the published
  tarball's binary set is asserted (AC-2b).
- **Missing served install scripts** — the one-liner 404s unless `install.ps1`/`install.sh` are
  uploaded to the R2 root and kept in sync; mitigated by the helper publishing them (AC-2c).
- **PATH not visible in the current shell** — a registry-only PATH write applies to new shells; for the
  `irm ... | iex` same-session case the installer also updates `$env:Path` in the current session
  (algorithm step 7) so `codex` is runnable immediately.
- **Credential leakage / retention growth** — least-privilege secret; retention policy.
- **Unix stub mistaken for a working installer** — explicit non-zero exit + clear message.
- **Redirect-plan coupling drift** — document the `/latest` contract + sequencing so the two plans
  don't diverge.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1 [code]** `publish-r2.mjs` run against a real `codex-<ver>-win32-x64.tgz` produces a
  `manifest.json` with `version` and a `win32-x64` object whose `sha256` and `size` match the tarball
  (verifiable by re-hashing), and a `latest` object whose body is exactly the version string.
  **Ordering:** `/latest` is written LAST, only after `{tarball, .sha256, manifest.json, install.ps1,
  install.sh}` are uploaded + verified; a simulated mid-publish failure leaves `/latest` unchanged
  (never pointing at an incomplete release).
- **AC-2 [code]** The helper is invoked from **both** `publish-sandbox-patch.md` Step 5 (primary) and
  `publish-npm.yml` (guarded), with no duplicated manifest logic. **Credential-absence is
  path-dependent:** the CI step no-ops cleanly when the R2 secret is absent, while the manual Step 5
  invocation **fails by default** when the credential is absent (unless `--skip-r2`/`--dry-run`) so a
  release cannot publish the GitHub asset while leaving the R2 one-liner broken. The required secret is
  named and scoped in the docs, and the chosen R2 upload interface (default `wrangler r2 object put`,
  env `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`/`R2_ACCOUNT_ID`/`R2_BUCKET`; S3-compatible PUT alternative with SigV4
  signing via `aws4fetch`/`@aws-sdk/client-s3`) is documented. **`wrangler` availability is explicit:**
  the helper uses a pinned `npx -y wrangler@<pinned>` (no global install assumed) and the CI workflow +
  manual Step 5 docs reflect that; the manual path hard-fails with a clear message if wrangler/network
  is unavailable.
- **AC-2b [code]** The published tarball's vendor tree contains the FULL Windows binary set —
  `codex.exe`, `codex-core.exe`, `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe`, `codex-command-runner.exe`, and
  `rg.exe` — asserted in the publish path (after the manual Step 5 binary-set reconciliation). A
  manifest written over an incomplete tarball must fail this check.
- **AC-2c [code]** After a publish run, `install.ps1` and `install.sh` exist at the R2 root keys
  `/install.ps1` and `/install.sh` and byte-match the repo `codex/scripts/install.{ps1,sh}` sources
  (the helper uploads/syncs them; verifiable in `--dry-run`/`--local-out` mode against a local target).
- **AC-3 [code]** `install.ps1` against a stub origin (`CODEX_BASE_URL`) with `CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1`
  resolves the version, downloads, verifies SHA-256, and lays out `CODEX_INSTALL_ROOT/bin`. PATH
  visibility is verified **two ways**: (a) **same session** — immediately after the script returns in
  the same PowerShell session (mimicking `irm ... | iex`), `codex --version` succeeds (the script
  updated `$env:Path`); (b) **persistent** — the user PATH registry value contains
  `<install_root>/bin` exactly once (so new shells inherit it). `rg.exe` is resolvable from that PATH
  entry and the extracted `bin/` binary set matches. (No interactive first-run during the test.)
- **AC-4 [code]** On a SHA-256 mismatch, `install.ps1` aborts with a clear error, deletes the temp
  download, and makes **no** change to the install dir or PATH (verified by diffing install dir + PATH
  before/after).
- **AC-5 [code]** Re-running `install.ps1` while a `codex`/`codex-core` whose exe path is under the
  install root is running: only those target-scoped processes are terminated (an unrelated `codex`
  process outside the install root is left running), the re-extract+swap succeeds (or rolls back on
  failure leaving the prior install intact), and exactly one `~/.codex-fork/bin` PATH entry remains
  (no duplicates).
- **AC-6 [code]** A non-version `/latest` body (HTML/error) makes `install.ps1` refuse to proceed
  (no download, clear error). The version guard accepts `0.135.0-copilot-api.1` and rejects HTML.
- **AC-7 [code]** `install.sh` exits non-zero with a clear Windows-only message and installs nothing.
- **AC-8 [code]** The plan/docs document that the redirect plan's `codex doctor` probe should curl
  `codex.evyatar.dev/latest` and that US-003 hints point at the `irm ... | iex` one-liner, plus the
  either-order sequencing note. (`doctor/updates.rs:24`, `tui/update_action.rs:17` named as the
  redirect plan's edit sites — not edited here.)
- **AC-9 [code]** `install.md` presents the one-liner as the primary unauthenticated install and keeps
  the authenticated path as the documented fallback; `docs/README.md` points at the one-liner.
- **AC-10 [code]** The plan/docs clearly partition operator/ops infra steps (bucket, DNS, credential)
  from code steps, so the operator knows exactly what to do by hand. The `## Infra Prerequisites`
  runbook exists and each AC is tagged `[code]` / `[infra]`.
- **AC-11 [code]** US-003 verifies whether the chosen `~/.codex-fork/bin` + `codex-package.json` layout
  is classified as a recognized layout by `install-context` (so `codex doctor`/self-update is not
  `None`). If it cannot be satisfied without a fixed standalone root, the doc records native self-update
  as an accepted v1 limitation (upgrade = re-run the one-liner) + a follow-up task.
- **AC-12 [infra, operator]** *(end-to-end, gated on infra)* With the bucket + DNS + credential in
  place and one real release published, `irm https://codex.evyatar.dev/install.ps1 | iex` on a clean
  Windows-x64 box yields a working PATH-wired `codex`. This AC is the operator's end-to-end validation,
  not a Ralph impl gate.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

- **US-001 — Shared release-publisher helper.** `codex/scripts/release/publish-r2.mjs`: sha256+size,
  write `manifest.json` + `latest`, **assert the tarball's full binary set**, upload release objects
  **and** sync `install.ps1`/`install.sh` to the R2 root via the chosen interface (default
  pinned `npx -y wrangler@<pinned> r2 object put`; S3-compatible alt needs a SigV4 signer dep
  `aws4fetch`/`@aws-sdk/client-s3`). **`/latest` written LAST** (partial-publish safe).
  `--dry-run`/`--local-out` mode; **path-dependent credential handling** (CI no-op vs manual hard-fail
  + wrangler/network prerequisite check). *Defines the manifest/latest contract.* (AC-1, AC-2b, AC-2c)
- **US-002 — Publish-flow wiring.** **Reconcile the manual Step 5 binary set** (add
  `codex-windows-sandbox-setup.exe` + `codex-command-runner.exe` cp at publish-sandbox-patch.md L304);
  call the helper from Step 5 (primary) + publish-npm.yml (guarded); name + scope the R2 secret in docs.
  Depends US-001. (AC-2)
- **US-003 — `install.ps1`.** Full algorithm: version guard (accepts `-copilot-api.N`), manifest fetch,
  sha verify + clean abort, **scoped** process-kill (exes under install root only), stage->backup->
  rename->rollback into `~/.codex-fork/bin/`, `rg.exe` co-location, `codex-package.json` marker,
  idempotent single PATH entry, install-context-classification verification (self-update consequence),
  noninteractive first-run, testability knobs. Depends US-001 (contract) + the prerequisite layout/URL
  decision. (AC-3..AC-6, AC-11)
- **US-004 — `install.sh` Windows-only stub.** Non-zero exit + clear message. Independent. (AC-7)
- **US-005 — `/latest` endpoint + doctor-probe contract.** Static-R2 `/latest` (produced by US-001) +
  doctor-probe/coupling doc; optional Worker deferred. Depends US-001. (AC-8)
- **US-006 — Docs + infra runbook.** `install.md`, `docs/README.md`, infra-vs-code runbook, redirect
  coupling note. Depends US-003 (for accurate install steps). (AC-9, AC-10)

## Suggested Decomposition

### Cluster: release-publish
- Stories: US-001, US-002
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: None
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`codex/scripts/release/publish-r2.mjs`,
  `codex/.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml`, `codex/.claude/commands/publish-sandbox-patch.md`];
  risk=medium (touches release/CI config — serialize internally: US-002 dependsOn US-001).
- `execution_mode` rationale: US-001 defines the manifest/latest contract that US-002 wires in;
  serialize within the cluster. The cluster's files don't overlap the installer or docs clusters.

### Cluster: installer-scripts
- Stories: US-003, US-004
- Phase: 1
- Depends on: release-publish (data/contract dependency only — US-003 consumes the manifest/latest
  shape; no file overlap, so it can author in parallel once the contract section is fixed)
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`codex/scripts/install.ps1`, `codex/scripts/install.sh`];
  risk=low.
- `execution_mode` rationale: install.ps1 and the Unix stub touch disjoint new files from the other
  clusters; parallel-safe at the file level.

### Cluster: endpoint-and-docs
- Stories: US-005, US-006
- Phase: 2
- Depends on: release-publish (US-005 needs `/latest`), installer-scripts (US-006 docs the install steps)
- File-overlap evidence: shared=[]; exclusive=[`codex/docs/workflows/install.md`,
  `codex/docs/README.md`, `codex/scripts/worker/` (optional)]; risk=low.
- `execution_mode` rationale: docs + endpoint contract land after the scripts exist so they describe
  real behavior; disjoint files from the other clusters.

## Open Questions

1. **Install layout — `~/.codex-fork/bin` (default) vs upstream standalone layout, with a self-update
   consequence.** The operator's `selected-direction.md` chose `~/.codex-fork/`. **Default: install under
   `~/.codex-fork/bin/` with a `codex-package.json` marker + co-located `rg.exe`; US-003 verifies
   whether `install-context/src/lib.rs` classifies this as a recognized layout.** If it does NOT (so
   `tui/src/update_action.rs:25` returns `UpdateAction::None`), **native `codex` self-update is a
   documented v1 limitation** — the upgrade path is re-running the one-liner — with a follow-up to add
   install-context support for `.codex-fork` or adopt the standalone layout
   (`~/.codex/packages/standalone/releases/...`). Operator may choose the standalone layout up front
   for native doctor/update. *Decision needed before US-003 starts.*
2. **Publish path placement.** Manual Step 5 is the primary uploader today (CI org-blocked). Should the
   CI `publish-npm.yml` R2 step land now (guarded/no-op without the secret) or be deferred until
   Actions are unblocked? **Default: land it guarded so it activates automatically when unblocked.**
3. **`/latest` shape — static R2 object vs Cloudflare Worker.** **Default: static object** (US-005);
   Worker deferred to a follow-up if single-origin redirect/logic is later wanted.
4. **Manifest URL shape** — direct custom-domain `codex.evyatar.dev/releases/<ver>/...` (default) vs a
   Worker-proxied path. Affects the `url` field the helper writes. *Decision needed before US-003 starts.*
5. **R2 upload interface** — **default `wrangler r2 object put`** (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`/
   `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`/`R2_BUCKET`) because it handles R2 auth natively (no hand-rolled SigV4); the
   S3-compatible PUT alternative needs a SigV4 signer dep (`aws4fetch`/`@aws-sdk/client-s3`). Operator
   confirms the interface + where the credential lives (CI secret and/or dev-box env).
6. **Retention policy** — how many releases to keep on the 10 GB free tier; manual prune vs publish-step
   prune. (Operator/ops decision; surfaced for the runbook.)
7. **Sequencing vs the redirect plan** — ship this installer first (then re-open the redirect plan's
   OQ1/US-003 to target `codex.evyatar.dev`), or let the redirect plan ship with neutralize/static
   defaults and treat this as the follow-up. Either order works; flag the coupling so they don't drift.

> **Resolved during Phase-4 review (no longer open):** the manual Step 5 binary-set gap is
> **confirmed** (publish-sandbox-patch.md L304 copies only `codex.exe`+`codex-core.exe`; CI packs all
> four at publish-npm.yml L139-142) and is now an **in-scope hard requirement** (US-002 + AC-2b), not an
> open question. The need to **publish `install.ps1`/`install.sh` to the R2 root** is now in-scope
> (US-001 + AC-2c).

<summary><strong>Phase 4 — Multi-model plan review (3 reviewers, 3 fix rounds, all 18 findings addressed)</strong></summary>

This plan was reviewed by three independent reviewers (Claude/Explore + Codex `gpt-5.5` + Copilot,
each effort=high with the severity rubric) and converged over three fix rounds. All 18 surfaced
findings (F-001..F-018) were addressed; the structured manifest is in `plan-review-findings.json` and
the per-round log is in `review-log.json`.

- **Round 1 (initial, 10 findings):** manual Step 5 packs only 2/4 binaries (consensus, confirmed by
  direct read); no R2 publish path for `install.ps1`/`install.sh` (consensus); flat `~/.codex-fork/`
  layout disables native self-update via install-context; over-broad process-kill; non-atomic Windows
  dir swap; weak AC-2/AC-3/AC-5; R2 mechanism + ordering underspecified.
- **Round 2 (re-review, 4 findings):** PATH same-session inconsistency (registry write vs child env);
  manual-path credential-absence too permissive; S3 PUT needs SigV4 signing; AC-3 PATH-visibility
  verification.
- **Round 3 (re-review, 4 findings):** US-001/Architecture wrangler contradiction; `wrangler`
  availability not specified for either publish path; partial-publish ordering (`/latest` must be
  written last); AC-2 wrangler-availability assertion.

Re-review cap (autonomous `max-re-reviews=2`) reached after rounds 2 and 3; convergence was productive
and non-plateauing (no repeated finding IDs). Remaining decisions are captured in `## Open Questions`
for the operator. **The plan is on HOLD for operator review before any implementation.**
